reddit_posts:
I think I have an honest to God phobia of waking up for school

I don't know what to do, it's hard to sleep and I'm in a lot of pain and I don't know why. My legs are constantly sore these days and I feel so dizzy.

The thing that's been driving me crazy lately is this overwhelming fear of waking up for school. It sounds ridiculous on the surface—just going to class—but it feels like a monster in my mind. Every time I try to fall asleep tonight, the image of my alarm clock goes off, and then having to get out of bed, walk across campus, and face everyone... it sends my heart racing so hard I can barely breathe.

I can see the light in my bedroom, hear the sound of the clock, but my legs feel like they're made of lead or maybe jelly—so heavy and unresponsive that I physically cannot move them. What’s one small thing you notice about your body when the dizziness starts, even if it’s just a tiny detail?

When the dizziness really kicks in—that moment where the room starts tilting—I notice my palms are sweating so much they're actually dripping onto my sheets. It's not a little pinch of sweat; it's like hot water pouring out. And right before that, just as the spinning starts, I feel this tightness in my chest, almost like someone is holding a vice grip around my ribs. 

It's terrifying because usually, I think I have control over my day. But right now, the alarm clock isn't just a timekeeper; it feels like an executioner's hammer.
